subject: SentryCare Dedicated commit — definitions & SLA redlines
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi.sharma@sentrycare.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal + capacity commit questions for SentryCare

Hi Aditi —

Thanks again for the time today. Attached is the updated pricing schedule (redwood_pricing_schedule_v2.xlsx) and a one-pager that maps the three commit tiers we discussed to expected GPU pool sizes and throughput ranges. A couple of quick clarifications we wanted to capture before legal redlines:  

- Definition ask: we currently use the term "Capacity Unit (CU)" in the quote to mean one vGPU-equivalent hour at our optimized serving profile for rtxA-series. We can change the language if you need a different baseline (e.g., per-GPU vs. per-vCPU).
- Throughput guarantee: our standard SLA states a 99th-percentile token-latency target per model variant, not a hard per-second throughput number. For committed pools we can commit a throughput floor (requests/sec) tied to a minimum pool size and a documented request profile.
- Credits & remedies: attached are our standard remedies. We are open to caps tied to the annual committed value but want to limit exposure for tail-load events.

Please review and let us know which of the three commit tiers you want to lock to the contract language and any specific throughput measurement method or workload profile you'd like us to use in the SLA.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_schedule_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), SentryCare_Dedicated_Commit_Term_SLA_Redlines.pdf (redlines PDF)

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Aditi Sharma <aditi.sharma@sentrycare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@sentrycare.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal + capacity commit questions for SentryCare

Ben —

Thanks for the docs. We shared the pricing with our procurement and legal and they pushed back on a few items. I've attached a redlined copy (SentryCare_Dedicated_Commit_Term_SLA_Redlines.pdf) with notes but the key open items are:  

1) Definition of "Capacity Unit": they want CU to be defined in terms of sustained throughput for a standard request profile (we run a mix of short chat + document-extract calls) and not GPU-hours. They argue per-GPU-hour can overstate cost if our real mix is latency-sensitive small-batch traffic.

2) Throughput guarantees: we need an explicit, measurable throughput floor (requests/minute or tokens/sec) for the committed pool plus a defined measurement window and traffic shaping rules for how you’ll count burst vs baseline.

3) Service credit cap: legal wants a simple cap (e.g., credits not to exceed 20% of monthly committed fees) and a clause that credits are the exclusive remedy.

4) Ramp & scaling: since this is a multi-quarter rollout, they want a ramp schedule for pool growth and an agreed method for re‑estimating CU needs each quarter.

Can your team redline the contract to replace the CU definition and provide a concrete throughput measurement method? If you can provide a short example of how credits would be calculated for a missed throughput floor, that would help speed approval.

Thanks,
Aditi
Director, Platform Engineering
SentryCare

-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SentryCare Dedicated commit — definitions & SLA redlines

Team —

Aditi's redlines came back from legal. The asks are reasonable but we should be careful with open-ended throughput floors and credit caps. Proposed internal positions below before we respond:  

- Capacity Unit (CU): offer a two-part definition: 1) baseline CU = one vGPU-hour at NTP-optimized profile (this preserves cost accounting on our side); 2) mapped CU for customer's profile = baseline CU adjusted by a workload coefficient established during onboarding measurement window (30 days). Put the mapping process in schedule rather than the core contract body.
- Throughput floor: offer a per-minute request floor for "typical profile" + an agreed 15-minute measurement window. Allow a defined burst allowance (e.g., 25% of baseline over 5 minutes) that is not counted against the floor.
- Credits cap: accept a hard cap at 20% of monthly committed fees but require the customer's remedy to be credit-only and limited to up to 3 consecutive months of credits across a 12-month period.
- Ramp schedule: propose quarterly rebaseline with a 30-day notice and a quarterly review meeting.

If everyone is comfortable I can send a reply proposing the two-part CU definition + an onboarding measurement schedule and an example calculation for a missed floor. Also recommends we attach the pricing workbook with tier math made explicit (I'll update with per-minute numbers).

Rishi
VP, Dedicated Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi.sharma@sentrycare.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal + capacity commit questions for SentryCare

Aditi —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the examples. We've ingested your asks and propose the following compromise items (summary):

1) Capacity Unit (CU): we'll use a two-part contract approach: the contract references a baseline CU (1 vGPU-hour at Redwood standard profile) but the SOW / onboarding schedule will contain a measured mapping from your production profile to CU-equivalents. That mapping is established during a 30-day onboarding evaluation where we'll run your typical mix and produce a conversion table (requests/minute -> CU/day).

2) Throughput guarantee: we will commit to a throughput floor defined as "sustained requests per minute for the customer's agreed profile" measured over rolling 15-minute windows. Bursts up to 25% over baseline within any 5-minute window will be excluded. We'll put the exact measurement script in the onboarding schedule and make logs available for audit for 30 days.

3) Service credits: we accept the 20% cap per month but with the following guardrails: credits are the exclusive monetary remedy; credits only apply if the failure is attributable to Redwood infrastructure (not customer misconfiguration), and credits are capped to apply for a maximum of 3 months per 12-month period.

4) Ramp & rebaseline: quarterly rebaseline with 30-day notice and a mutually agreed updated mapping to CU. Changes to committed CU that increase cost will be billable; reductions will be applied prospectively.

Attached: redwood_pricing_schedule_v2.xlsx (updated with per-minute math) and a short illustration in the SOW template. If that sounds OK I'll ask legal to incorporate language and send a tracked redline for SentryCare legal to review.

Example credit calc (included inline): 
- Monthly committed fee: $120,000
- Throughput floor missed for 10% of hours in month => credit = 10% * monthly fee limited to 20% cap => $12,000 (subject to cap)

Wanted to flag to Rishi/Marissa: if SentryCare insists on unbounded measurement/sla windows or removes the attribution clause, we should push back hard.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Sales

-----Original Message-----
From: Aditi Sharma <aditi.sharma@sentrycare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@sentrycare.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SentryCare Dedicated commit — definitions & SLA redlines

Ben / team —

Thanks for the pragmatic reply and the example calc — that helps. A few follow-ups from our legal/procurement:  

- We still need the on-paper definition of the "measurement script" and the log format (JSON lines with timestamps, request id, latency, token_count). Can you commit to the log schema in the SOW?
- We need the measurement window explicit in the contract (15-minute rolling) and a statement that Redwood will not use a different internal sampling method to invalidate measurements.
- On credits: the 3-month consecutive cap is acceptable if you also add a clause that credits are applied within 30 days of validated event and do not require escalation to execs to trigger.

If you can get legal to add the log schema and acceptance timeline, we can finish the commercial review and send to procurement for signature.

Regards,
Aditi

-----Original Message-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SentryCare Dedicated commit — definitions & SLA redlines

Quick internal next steps:  

1) Priya — please ask Legal to include the measurement script stub and the log schema in the SOW schedule (we'll provide the exact JSON-lines format). Also add the 15-minute rolling-window language and the 25% burst carve-out.
2) Marissa — update the pricing workbook to show the per-minute baseline numbers for each tier and include the example credit calc Ben provided.
3) Karthik — confirm the onboarding runbook (30-day evaluation) and that our telemetry can produce the log output for audit. If there are infra gaps, flag them now.

If we get the SOW addendum with schema + the updated workbook, I'll send the tracked redline to SentryCare legal and aim to have signatures by end of next week.

Rishi
VP, Dedicated Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
